findings.summary: Soundness: the group bound is too coarse to measure whether a job fits one producer run. All code (any number of crates, tests and xtask) counts as one group, and only a reading spanning all four groups is refused. The 30-deliverable backstop is far above both failed jobs (9 and 11).
findings.evidence: The accepted reading set the bound at 'above 8 deliverables or 4 surfaces', with each crates/<crate>, xtask and tests counted as its own surface. That bound would have refused both real jobs. The candidate weakened it to 3-of-4 coarse groups and 30 deliverables, and Athena's replay found 0 of 50 readings newly refused. A finer measure catches zaj2 while keeping focused jobs: per-crate surfaces, or a lower deliverable bound calibrated against the two real failed readings rather than invented ones.

summary: The change adds a check_job_size step to the reading gate (refusing_check), with unit tests, refusal corpus cases and a CHANGELOG entry. The targeted tests and the corpus pass when I run them, and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test results pass. But the check does not prevent the failure class across both cited jobs. The real reading of job 20261017-205554-zaj2 in the evidence records spans code, config and docs with 11 deliverables besides CHANGELOG, so the candidate's rule accepts it: it refuses only readings that span all four groups or have more than 30 deliverables. The test passes only because its zaj2 fixture invents a CI workflow, xtask files and extra docs the job never listed. The doc comment also wrongly says zaj2 spanned four groups. The accepted reading's own bound (more than 8 deliverables or 4 finer surfaces) would have refused both jobs; the implementation weakened it. Verdict: fail.
